newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sugar content said rising in Australian cane.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sugar content said rising in Australian cane.

text.p: Improved sugar content in Queensland cane this season could return increased income of A$43 million on a harvest of 36 million tonnes of cane, the Australian Cane Farmers Association Ltd (ACFA) said.
Cane varieties bred by the Bureau of Sugar Experiment Stations had performed much better than expected for the 1996 season, ACFA deputy manager David Crawford said in a statement

Recent crushing statistics showed that sugar levels in cane were much higher this season than last, mainly because of the use of better varieties, seasonal influences and improved management practices, he said.
The upward trend in sugar content in cane (CCS - commercial cane sugar) had continued since 1990 after an earlier trend downward, Crawford said.
Queensland's state average CCS so far this year had risen to 13.66 percent from about 13.35 percent this time last year, he said.

The difference in CCS was valued at close to A$1.20 a tonne of cane based on a sugar price of A$340.00 a tonne. This would conservatively translate to about A$43 million if the Queensland harvest was about 36 million tonnes of cane, he said.
